content.title: Tagger denies Shi from 4-2 down in decider to reach Guangzhou semis
content.description: No. 4 seed Lilli Tagger came from 4-2 down in the third set to defeat wild card Shi Han 6-4, 3-6, 7-5 in 2 hours and 38 minutes in the Guangzhou Open quarterfinals, converting her second match point to reach her third career tour-level semifinal. The 18-year-old Austrian joins 16-year-old Sun Xinran in the last four -- they are the youngest pair of WTA semifinalists at a single tournament (in terms of combined age) since 17-year-olds Olga Danilovic and Anastasia Potapova met in the 2018 Moscow River Cup final.

content.title: Hot shot: Sun Xinran thrills Guangzhou crowd with 'astounding defense'
content.description: Sixteen-year-old wild card Sun Xinran showed off some incredible speed -- and then perfect control on the final scooped lob -- to steal this point from Claire Liu in the Guangzhou Open quarterfinals.

content.title: Six set points saved! Wild card Sun, 16, denies Liu to make Guangzhou semis
content.description: Junior No. 1 Sun Xinran's dream start to her tour-level career continued in the Guangzhou Open quarterfinals as the 16-year-old wild card saved six set points in the second set to defeat Claire Liu 7-5, 7-6(2) in 2 hours and 1 minute. In just her second WTA main draw, the No. 405-ranked teenager advanced to her first semifinal.

content.title: Shnaider repeats Ningbo win over Eala in 2:52 Tokyo blockbuster
content.description: No. 3 seed Diana Shnaider defeated No. 8 seed Alexandra Eala for the second time in as many weeks in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis quarterfinals, backing up her Ningbo second-round win with a 2-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 victory in 2 hours and 52 minutes to reach her fifth semifinal of 2026.

content.title: Quevedo tops Teichmann in Guangzhou; into second SF in past three events
content.description: Sao Paulo champion Kaitlin Quevedo has now won eight of her last nine matches after defeating Jil Teichmann 7-6(2), 6-3 in the Guangzhou Open quarterfinals, advancing to her second tour-level semifinal.

content.title: Dart bests Badosa in Guangzhou three-setter; into second WTA semifinal
content.description: Qualifier Harriet Dart reached the second tour-level semifinal of her career (following Cluj-Napoca 2024) with a 3-6, 6-2, 6-4 defeat of No. 5 seed Paula Badosa in the Guangzhou Open quarterfinals.

content.title: Pohankova, 18, defeats Parks in Tokyo to reach first WTA semifinal
content.description: Playing the fourth WTA main draw of her career, 18-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova reached her first semifinal with a 7-6(3), 6-3 defeat of qualifier Alycia Parks in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis quarterfinals.

content.title: Tagger speeds past Linette in 67 minutes to make Guangzhou quarters
content.description: No. 4 seed Lilli Tagger enjoyed her second 6-2, 6-2 victory in a row at the Guangzhou Open, defeating Magda Linette by the same scoreline as she had beaten Venus Williams in the first round to reach her fourth tour-level quarterfinal of 2026.

content.title: Quevedo pulls away from Bondar in Guangzhou to make second WTA quarterfinal
content.description: Sao Paulo champion Kaitlin Quevedo reached her second career tour-level quarterfinal at the Guangzhou Open after defeating Anna Bondar 7-5, 6-3 in the second round.

content.title: From match point down, 16-year-old Sun beats Timofeeva to make Guangzhou QF
content.description: Chinese wild card Sun Xinran, 16, reached her first WTA quarterfinal at the Guangzhou Open after coming from 5-2 down in the third set to defeat No. 7 seed Maria Timofeeva, who held one match point at 5-3 but double faulted. Junior No. 1 Sun was contesting her second WTA main draw after making the Beijing third round three weeks ago.

content.title: Rybakina wins all-Kazakhstani derby vs. Putintseva to make Tokyo quarters
content.description: No. 1 seed Elena Rybakina improved to 3-2 against Kazakhstani compatriot Yulia Putintseva with a 6-2, 6-3 victory over the qualifier in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second round.

content.title: Slovak wild card Pohankova, 18, stuns Osaka in Tokyo for first Top 20 win
content.description: In her first career meeting with a Top 20 player, 18-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova upset No. 7 seed Naomi Osaka 6-3, 7-5 in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second round. The Slovak teenager, who was the 2025 Wimbledon junior champion, advanced to her second quarterfinal in her fourth WTA main draw, and first at WTA 500 level.

content.title: Hot shots: Two 'sensational' short angles by Mia Pohankova in Tokyo
content.description: Mia Pohankova, 18, came up with two of her most creative winners on key points en route to her first Top 20 win over Naomi Osaka in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second round -- a pair of unexpected short forehand angles to convert both break point ar 3-3 and then set point.

content.title: Fernandez saves two set points, beats Mertens for second straight week
content.description: Leylah Fernandez defeated Elise Mertens for a second week in a row to reach her sixth quarterfinal of 2026 at the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis, backing up her 2-6, 6-3, 7-5 Ningbo first-round win with a 6-2, 7-6(8) victory in Tokyo. Fernandez held off a late Mertens charge from 4-1 down in the second set, and saved two set points in the tiebreak. She improved to 3-2 overall against the Belgian.

content.title: Parks beats Birrell in Tokyo to reach fourth quarterfinal of season
content.description: Qualifier Alycia Parks needed just 1 hour, 12 minutes to defeat lucky loser Kimberly Birrell 6-3, 6-1 and reach the quarterfinals of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Thursday. Parks, who is into her fourth quarterfinal of the season, will next face either No. 7 seed Naomi Osaka or Mia Pohankova.

content.title: Venus Williams reaches first doubles semifinal since 2016 alongside Tjen in Guangzhou
content.description: Venus Williams and Janice Tjen dropped just four games in their Guangzhou quarterfinal win over Lyudmyla Kichenok and Makoto Ninomiya on Wednesday night, advancing to the last four and giving Williams her first doubles semifinal appearance in a decade.

Hot shot: Talia Gibson clubs a forehand to save match point in Tokyo
content.description: Down but not quite out: trailing Alexandra Eala 5-0 in the third set of their Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second-round tilt, Talia Gibson came out on top of the best point of the match, ending a bruising 24-shot exchange by clubbing a forehand winner into the opposite corner.

content.title: Wild card Shi tops Yastremska to make first WTA quarterfinal in Guangzhou
content.description: Chinese wild card Shi Han saved one set point in the first set en route to defeating qualifier Dayana Yastremska 7-5, 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open second round, advancing to her first career WTA quarterfinal.

content.title: Eala comes from a set down vs. Gibson to make Tokyo quarterfinals
content.description: No. 8 seed Alexandra Eala improved to 3-0 against Talia Gibson with a 4-6, 6-2, 6-0 victory in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second round to advance to her sixth tour-level quarterfinal of 2026.

content.title: Dart upsets Tjen in Guangzhou; into first WTA quarterfinal since 2024
content.description: Qualifier Harriet Dart defeated No. 2 seed Janice Tjen 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 in the Guangzhou Open second round to notch her second Top 50 win of 2026. The Briton advanced to her first tour-level quarterfinal since Eastbourne 2024 and the first of her career on outdoor hard courts.

content.title: Osaka champ Siniakova bests Tararudee in Guangzhou, extends win streak
content.description: Freshly-crowned Osaka champion Katerina Siniakova extended her winning streak to six matches after defeating No. 3 seed Lanlana Tararudee 2-6, 6-1, 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open first round. Siniakova held off a late charge by Tararudee from 5-1 to 5-4 in the third set.

content.title: From 3-1 down in decider, Joint overcomes Bucsa to make Tokyo quarters
content.description: Qualifier Maya Joint levelled her head-to-head against Cristina Bucsa at 1-1 with a 6-1, 2-6, 6-4 victory in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis second round, advancing to her third quarterfinal of 2026 (and second at WTA 500 level).

content.title: Rakhimova edges Alexandrova in deciding tiebreak to reach Tokyo quarters
content.description: Lucky loser Kamilla Rakhimova battled past Ekaterina Alexandrova 6-4, 4-6, 7-6(5) in 2 hours and 51 minutes to reach the quarterfinals of the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis, improving to 2-0 in their head-to-head. Rakhimova advanced to her third career WTA 500 quarterfinal.

content.title: 'The deadly touch of Sawangkaew' ends lung-busting rally in Guangzhou
content.description: A perfectly executed drop shot isn't easy after a 24-shot rally, but Manachaya Sawangkaew pulled it off Tuesday night in Guangzhou. Catching Sun Xinran off balance with a deft touch, she erased a late game point to stay within striking distance.

content.title: Paolini turns up the heat with drop shot-lob masterclass against Osaka in Tokyo
content.description: A first-round showdown between Jasmine Paolini and Naomi Osaka delivered no shortage of quality, and this point was among the finest. Though Osaka ultimately earned the win on home soil in Tokyo, Paolini dazzled with a perfectly executed forehand drop shot-backhand lob combo for a winner.

metadata.credit: ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP via Getty Images

content.title: Sakatsume gets her steps in with quartet of quality scrambles in Tokyo
content.description: Though she came up short against Leylah Fernandez on Tuesday in Tokyo, Himeno Sakatsume gave the home fans plenty to cheer about, turning defense into entertainment with a series of impressive full-court scrambles.

metadata.credit: Andrew CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP via Getty Images

content.title: Sorribes Tormo keeps Sonmez guessing with volley magic in Guangzhou
content.description: Challenge Sara Sorribes Tormo at the net at your own risk. Zeynep Sonmez learned that lesson Tuesday in Guangzhou, as the Spaniard produced a pair of brilliant volley winners. In the end, though, Sonmez emerged with a three-set victory.

content.title: 'That's Harry Potter stuff': Putintseva dips into her bag of tricks in Tokyo
content.description: Yulia Putintseva put her full arsenal on display in Tuesday's three-set win over Maria Sakkari in Tokyo, mixing blistering forehands, deft drop shots, perfectly timed lobs and even a one-handed passing shot to set up match point.

content.title: Junior No. 1 Sun Xinran continues surge, tops Sawangkaew in Guangzhou
content.description: Wild card Sun Xinran, 16, scored her second career Top 100 win to defeat Mananchaya Sawangkaew 6-3, 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open first round. Junior No. 1 Sun, the reigning US Open girls' champion, reached the third round of Beijing on her WTA main-draw debut three weeks ago, and followed it by winning the World Tennis Tour Junior Finals in Chengdu last week.

content.title: Tagger strikes 29 winners in 16 games, defeats Venus Williams in Guangzhou
content.description: No. 4 seed Lilli Tagger hit 29 winners in a 6-2, 6-2 victory over former world No. 1 Venus Williams in the first round of the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Tagger will next face Poland’s Magda Linette for a place in the quarterfinals.

content.title: Liu saves two match points, denies Ruzic in 2:51 Guangzhou marathon
content.description: American Claire Liu saved two match points late in the second set to defeat Antonia Ruzic 4-6, 7-6, 6-4 in the first round of the Guangzhou Open. Liu will next face the winner of the match between No. 3 seed Lanlana Tararudee and Katerina Siniakova.

content.title: Osaka saves triple set point vs. Paolini, advances to Tokyo second round
content.description: Former champion and No. 7 seed Naomi Osaka saved three set points late in the second before overcoming Jasmine Paolini 6-3, 7-6 to reach the second round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. Osaka will next meet Mia Pohankova for a spot in the last eight.

content.title: Pohankova bests Valentova in 70-minute all-teenage Tokyo tussle
content.description: Eighteen-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova defeated qualifier Tereza Valentova 6-1, 6-4 to advance to the second round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. She will next face former champion and No. 7 seed Naomi Osaka.

content.title: Five match points saved! Yastremska escapes Volynets in Guangzhou thriller
content.description: Ukraine’s Dayana Yastremska staged a remarkable comeback from 5-2 down in the final set, saving five match points to defeat No. 8 seed Katie Volynets 7-5, 1-6, 7-6 in the first round of the Guangzhou Open. Yastremska will next face Han Shi in the second round.

content.title: Sasnovich survives twists and turns in Tokyo, bests Bartunkova in three sets
content.description: Qualifier Aliaksandra Sasnovich needed 2 hours, 40 minutes to defeat Nikola Bartunkova 6-4, 6-7, 6-3 in the first round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. Sasnovich will next face No. 3 seed Diana Shnaider for a place in the quarterfinals.

content.title: Fernandez withstands Sakatsume hot shots to advance in Tokyo
content.description: Ningbo runner-up Leylah Fernandez defeated wild card Himeno Sakatsume 6-2, 6-4 in the first round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. Fernandez will next face No. 5 seed Elise Mertens for a place in the quarterfinals. The pair are tied 2-2 in their head-to-head series.

content.title: Sonmez outlasts Sorribes Tormo in three sets to make Guangzhou second round
content.description: No. 6 seed Zeynep Sonmez overcame a second-set lapse to defeat Sara Sorribes Tormo 6-1, 4-6, 6-2 in the first round of the Guangzhou Open. Sonmez will next face Swiss player Jil Teichmann.

content.title: Putintseva wins fifth edition of rivalry vs. Sakkari in Tokyo three-setter
content.description: Kazakhstan’s Yulia Putintseva defeated former world No. 3 Maria Sakkari 6-4, 3-6, 6-1 in the first round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. Putintseva now leads Sakkari 3-2 in their head-to-head series and will next face world No. 1 and compatriot Elena Rybakina.

content.title: Bucsa snaps losing streak, pulls away from Parry in Tokyo opener
content.description: Spain’s Cristina Bucsa snapped a four-match losing streak with a 7-5, 6-1 victory over France’s Diane Parry in the first round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. Bucsa will next face Australia’s Maya Joint for a place in the quarterfinals.

content.title: Quevedo ousts former champ Kenin in 2:41 Guangzhou marathon
content.description: Spain’s Kaitlin Quevedo defeated former champion Sofia Kenin 6-4, 6-7(5), 6-4 in 2 hours, 41 minutes to advance to the second round of the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Quevedo will next face Anna Bondar for a place in the quarterfinals.

content.title: Hot shot: Jil Teichmann's half-volleyed pickup in Guangzhou
content.description: Jil Teichmann found a marvellous half-volleyed pickup en route to defeating Simona Waltert in an all-Swiss first round at the Guangzhou Open.

content.title: Linette saves two set points, advances past Zakharova in Guangzhou
content.description: Poland’s Magda Linette saved two set points en route to a 7-6, 6-4 victory over Anastasia Zakharova in the first round of the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Linette will next face either No. 4 seed Lilli Tagger or former world No. 1 Venus Williams.

content.title: Joint upsets Cirstea in Tokyo for second time in 2026
content.description: Qualifier Maya Joint upset No. 6 seed Sorana Cirstea 6-3, 7-6 to advance to the second round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Tuesday. Joint will next face Spain’s Cristina Bucsa for a place in the quarterfinals.

content.title: Tjen, Venus Williams sweep into Guangzhou quarterfinals in doubles debut
content.description: Playing her first match since the US Open, Venus Williams teamed with Janice Tjen to defeat Ekaterine Gorgodze and Kimberly Zimmerman 6-0, 7-5 in 70 minutes on Monday night and advance to the Guangzhou quarterfinals.

thumbnail.title: Janice Tjen and Venus Williams, Guangzhou 2026

content.title: Dart battles past Prozorova in all-qualifier first round in Guangzhou
content.description: An all-qualifier first round at the Guangzhou Open saw Harriet Dart defeat Singapore semifinalist Tatiana Prozorova 6-4, 2-6, 6-2 in 2 hours and 15 minutes.

content.title: Badosa holds off Lee to reach Guangzhou second round
content.description: No. 5 seed Paula Badosa defeated American qualifier Carol Young Suh Lee 6-1, 6-4 in the Guangzhou Open first round.

content.title: Eala's experience shines to defeat teenage wild card Stojsavljevic in Tokyo
content.description: No. 8 seed Alexandra Eala needed just 75 minutes to defeat 17-year-old British wild card Mika Stojsavljevic 6-1, 6-2 in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis first round.

content.title: In-form Shi defeats Ibragimova in straight sets in Guangzhou opener
content.description: Chinese wild card Shi Han continued her strong Asian Swing with a 6-4, 6-4 defeat of qualifier Alevtina Ibragimova in the Guangzhou Open first round, avenging a 6-3, 2-6, 6-2 loss to Ibragimova in the Huzhou WTA 125 first round in April.

content.title: Mertens bests home hope Uchijima in straight sets in Tokyo first round
content.description: No. 5 seed Elise Mertens improved to 3-0 against Japanese wild card Moyuka Uchijima with a 6-4, 6-2 victory in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis first round.

content.title: Hot shot: Moyuka Uchijima finds the space to win cat-and-mouse rally in Tokyo
content.description: Both players' reflexes and creativity were on show in this cat-and-mouse exchange between Moyuka Uchijima and Elise Mertens in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis first round, but it was Uchijima who ultimately found the space to slot a winning backhand pass past the Belgian.

content.title: Bondar upsets top seed Snigur in Guangzhou first round
content.description: Anna Bondar improved to 2-0 against Daria Snigur with a 6-4, 6-2 upset of the No. 1 seed in the Guangzhou Open first round. Bondar's previous win was six years ago on clay, in the 2020 Prague WTA 125 first round.

content.title: Gibson survives tight second set vs. Kasatkina in all-Australian Tokyo opener
content.description: In an all-Australian first-round derby at the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis, Talia Gibson won the first eight games against qualifier Daria Kasatkina -- but had to fight hard in the second set to close out a 6-0, 7-5 victory.

content.title: Hot shots: Three perfect passes by Daria Kasatkina in Tokyo
content.description: Daria Kasatkina showed off some tremendous anticipation to foil Talia Gibson with these three passing shots in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis first round.

content.title: Timofeeva wins 11 of last 13 games to defeat Kostovic in Guangzhou
content.description: No. 7 seed Maria Timofeeva came from 3-1 down in the first set to defeat qualifier Teodora Kostovic 6-4, 6-1 in the Guangzhou Open first round.

content.title: Kraus defeats Udvardy in straight sets in Guangzhou first round
content.description: Sinja Kraus improved to 2-1 against Panna Udvardy to win their first hard-court meeting 6-4, 6-2 in the Guangzhou Open first round.

content.title: Parks saves three set points, holds off Wang Xinyu in Tokyo first round
content.description: Qualifier Alycia Parks saved three set points in the second set -- one trailing 5-4 and two in the tiebreak -- to defeat Wang Xinyu 6-1, 7-6(7) in the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis first round. Parks improved to 2-0 against Wang.

content.title: Champions Reel: How Elena Rybakina won Ningbo 2026
content.description: No. 1 seed Elena Rybakina captured her 15th career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title, eighth on outdoor hard courts and fourth of the season at the 2026 BNB Ningbo Open. The tournament was Rybakina's first successful title defense of her career, and her first trophy as World No. 1.

content.title: Champions Reel: How Katerina Siniakova won Osaka 2026
content.description: Ranked No. 86, Katerina Siniakova captured her sixth career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title, fourth on outdoor hard courts and first since Nanchang 2023 at the 2026 Kinoshita Group Japan Open.

content.title: Elena Rybakina locks in on WTA Finals after successful Ningbo defense
content.description: With a fourth trophy of 2026 secured, Elena Rybakina breaks down her week-over-week progression in China and the mindset powering her drive toward the season finale.

thumbnail.title: NINGBO - POST MATCH INTERVIEW - FINAL - ELENA RYBAKINA - ENGLISH_Digital Download_m52735

content.title: Rybakina beats Fernandez to defend Ningbo Open title
content.description: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina defeated Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 to win the BNB Ningbo Open title on Sunday. The victory marks Rybakina's fourth title of the 2026 season, the most by any player this year, and the 15th singles title of her career.

content.title: Siniakova wins Osaka final to claim sixth career title
content.description: Katerina Siniakova maintained her perfect record against Ashlyn Krueger, defeating the American 6-1, 6-0 to win the Japan Open title in Osaka on Sunday. With the victory, Siniakova improved to 5-0 in her head-to-head record against Krueger and claimed the sixth WTA singles title of her career.

content.title: Rybakina holds off Shnaider's late charge to reach second straight Ningbo final
content.description: Elena Rybakina needed 11 set points to take the opener against Diana Shnaider on Saturday night and weathered a late push after failing to serve out the match, reaching a second straight Ningbo final and keeping her title defense alive.

content.title: Siniakova scrambles to earn key break point in penultimate game of Osaka semis
content.description: Katerina Siniakova needed seven break points to earn the decisive break against Katie Boulter in their Osaka semifinal Saturday night. She created the final opportunity with a dazzling defensive scramble that ended in a running forehand winner.

content.title: Fernandez extends strong form in Ningbo, outduels Bouzkova to reach 10th career final
content.description: Leylah Fernandez continued her strong form during the Asian Swing on Saturday night, defeating Marie Bouzkova 6-3, 7-5 in 1 hour, 58 minutes to reach her second final of the stretch and the 10th of her career.

content.title: Siniakova defeats Boulter in Osaka semis to reach first WTA singles final since 2023
content.description: Katerina Siniakova ended a three-year wait for another tour-level singles final Saturday night in Osaka, defeating Katie Boulter 6-1, 6-4 in 1 hour, 25 minutes to reach her first championship match since Jiangxi 2023.

content.title: Krueger edges Li in all-American clash to reach second Osaka final
content.description: Ashlyn Krueger let a second-set lead slip away but regrouped to outlast fellow American and top seed Ann Li on Saturday night, advancing to her third career final and second in Osaka.

content.title: Rybakina pushes past Kawa in three sets to reach Ningbo semifinals
content.description: Elena Rybakina weathered a second-set dip before regaining control to defeat Katarzyna Kawa 6-1, 3-6, 6-1 in 1 hour, 45 minutes on Friday night and return to the Ningbo semifinals. The victory marked her first completed match win as World No. 1.

content.title: Behind the curtain: Victoria Mboko on her idol, proudest moment and favorite quote
content.description: Go off-court with Victoria Mboko as she opens up about the player who inspired her, her proudest career milestone, her guiding quote, and how listening to music keeps her calm before big matches.

content.title: Shnaider battles past Jovic in three-set thriller to make Ningbo semis
content.description: No. 6 seed Diana Shnaider booked her spot in her fourth semifinal of 2026 after overcoming No. 4 seed Iva Jovic 6-3, 4-6, 6-1 in 2 hours and 11 minutes in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals. Shnaider, the 2023 Ningbo runner-up, levelled her head-to-head against Jovic at 1-1.

content.title: Hot shot: Diana Shnaider blends touch and power to win riveting Ningbo rally
content.description: Diana Shnaider blended full-on power with clever short slices to out-manoeuvre Iva Jovic in this exchange in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals -- then finished with a backhand banger to take control of their deciding set.

content.title: Full match replay: Baptiste erases six match points to upset Sabalenka in Madrid
content.description: Down on the brink against the top seed, Hailey Baptiste stages a high-wire escape to prevail 2-6, 6-2, 7-6 (6) and reach her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

thumbnail.title: Full match replay: Baptiste erases six match points to upset Sabalenka in Madrid
thumbnail.description: Down on the brink against the top seed, Hailey Baptiste stages a high-wire escape to prevail 2-6, 6-2, 7-6 (6) and reach her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

content.title: Hot shot: Iva Jovic's 23-shot lung-buster to seal set point in Ningbo
content.description: Iva Jovic levelled the match against Diana Shnaider at one set all in spectacular fashion in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals -- a 23-stroke line-to-line lung-buster which she turned in her favor with a canny drop shot and then a forehand pass on the stretch.

content.title: Hot shot: Diana Shnaider holds firm to defend the net in Ningbo
content.description: There was no backing down for Diana Shnaider in this point against Iva Jovic in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals -- holding firm at net, she pulled off a series of brilliant reflex volleys before putting away a firm overhead.

content.title: From a set and a break down, Boulter escapes Ruzic to make Osaka semis
content.description: No. 8 seed Katie Boulter booked her place in her third tour-level semifinal of 2026 after coming from 6-3, 2-0 down to defeat Antonia Ruzic 3-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the Kinoshita Group Japan Open quarterfinals.

content.title: Hot shot: Ekaterina Alexandrova measures the sharpest angles in Ningbo
content.description: A canny forehand slice, followed by the sharpest of forehand angles to open the court and an equally precise backhand angle for the pass -- Ekaterina Alexandrova showed off her full range in this point against Leylah Fernandez in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals.

content.title: Fernandez wins sixth edition of rivalry vs. Alexandrova; into Ningbo semis
content.description: Leylah Fernandez levelled her head-to-head with Ekaterina Alexandrova at 3-3 with a 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 victory in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals -- her second defeat of Alexandrova in as many weeks, following a 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 win in the Wuhan first round. Singapore champion Fernandez advanced to her second semifinal of 2026, and she has now won 12 of her last 15 matches.

content.title: Hot shot: Katerina Siniakova's pass on the stretch in Osaka
content.description: Katerina Siniakova was stretched out wide and caught off balance by Mary Stoiana's angled chip in the Kinoshita Group Japan Open quarterfinals -- but the Czech nonetheless produced a perfect forehand pass down the line to snatch the point.

content.title: Siniakova eases past Stoiana in Osaka; into first semifinal in 13 months
content.description: Katerina Siniakova defeated American qualifier Mary Stoiana 6-1, 6-2 in 1 hour and 11 minutes in the Kinoshita Group Japan Open quarterfinals, advancing to her first tour-level semifinal since Seoul 2025.

content.title: Bouzkova triumphs over Bejlek in all-Czech quarterfinal derby in Ningbo
content.description: A first-time meeting between two Czech compatriots in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals saw Marie Bouzkova defeat Sara Bejlek 6-3, 6-4 to reach her third tour-level semifinal of 2026, and first at WTA 500 level or above since Monterrey 2025.

content.title: Hot shots: Bouzkova breaks down absurd Bejlek defense at net in Ningbo
content.description: What does it take to get past Sara Bejlek? Marie Bouzkova had to work overtime to finish off these two points at net against her Czech compatriot in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals.

content.title: Hot shots: Two ridiculous reflex winners by Sara Bejlek in Ningbo
content.description: Sara Bejlek produced two incredible reflex winners against Marie Bouzkova in the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals -- first on offense as she pulled off a ridiculous diving, angled stretch volley; and second on defense as she blocked a Bouzkova smash back past her Czech compatriot.

content.title: Former champ Krueger returns to Osaka semis with 61-minute rout of Gibson
content.description: Ashlyn Krueger returned to the Kinoshita Group Japan Open semifinals for the first time since her 2023 title run with a 6-1, 6-3 defeat of No. 4 seed Talia Gibson in just 61 minutes. Krueger will next bid to defeat No. 1 seed Ann Li for the first time in the American compatriots' third meeting.

content.title: Li edges Tagger in third-set tiebreak to reach Osaka semifinals
content.description: In a match that featured just two breaks of serve over 2 hours and 11 minutes, No. 1 seed Ann Li edged Lilli Tagger 6-4, 3-6, 7-6(0) in the Kinoshita Group Japan Open quarterfinals to book her spot in her third semifinal of 2026.

content.title: Full match replay: Sabalenka's unshakeable serve anchors win vs. Rybakina in Miami
content.description: A flawless second-serve performance and heavy first-strike returns allow Aryna Sabalenka to pull away for a commanding 6-4, 6-3 win.

thumbnail.title: Full match replay: Sabalenka's unshakeable serve anchors win vs. Rybakina in Miami
thumbnail.description: A flawless second-serve performance and heavy first-strike returns allow Aryna Sabalenka to pull away for a commanding 6-4, 6-3 win.

content.title: Full match replay: Gauff overcomes Andreeva in three-set Rome showdown

content.title: Shnaider closes out Eala on seventh match point; into Ningbo quarters
content.description: No. 6 seed and 2023 BNB Ningbo Open finalist Diana Shnaider returned to the quarterfinals for a third time with a 7-5, 6-4 defeat of Alexandra Eala, closing out the first-time pro encounter on her seventh match point.

content.title: Kawa stuns Bencic in Ningbo to score first career Top 20 win
content.description: At the age of 33, qualifier Katarzyna Kawa scored her first career Top 20 win with a 7-5, 6-2 upset of No. 5 seed Belinda Bencic in the BNB Ningbo Open second round. The Pole advanced to her first tour-level quarterfinal on hard courts, and her first at WTA 500 level or above.

content.title: Block party: Kawa repels two Bencic smashes, finds the line in Ningbo
content.description: Katarzyna Kawa came up with a pair of brilliant blocks of Belinda Bencic's smashes in this BNB Ningbo Open second-round point, with the second landing on the sideline for a winner.

content.title: Siniakova wins seventh edition of rivalry vs. Linette; into Osaka quarters
content.description: Katerina Siniakova lost her first three encounters with Magda Linette between 2012 and 2019, but has now won all four since 2022 after defeating the Pole 6-4, 6-1 in the Kinoshita Group Japan Open second round. The result was Siniakova's second victory in the series in the past month, having also defeated Linette 6-4, 6-3 in the Beijing first round. Siniakova advanced to her first quarterfinal of 2026.

content.title: Jovic wins fourth edition of rivalry vs. Paolini to reach Ningbo quarters
content.description: No. 4 seed Iva Jovic defeated Italy’s Jasmine Paolini 6-4, 6-3 on Thursday to advance to the quarterfinals of the BNB Ningbo Open, levelling their head-to-head at 2-2. Jovic will face the winner of the match between No. 6 seed Diana Shnaider and Alexandra Eala in the next round.
